title: Simultaneous K-flat realization of a commuting two-family scalar diagram
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $(B_N)_{N\geq1}$ and $(D_j)_{j\geq1}$ inverse systems of commutative ring sheaves with transition maps $b_{N,M}$ and $d_{j,k}$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Fix $e\geq1$, maps $\beta_N:R\to B_N$, $\delta_j:R\to D_j$, and $q_{N,j}:B_N\to D_j$ for $eN\geq j$. Assume $q_{N,j}\beta_N=\delta_j$, $b_{N,M}\beta_N=\beta_M$, $d_{j,k}\delta_j=\delta_k$, $q_{M,j}b_{N,M}=q_{N,j}$ when $N\geq M$ and $eM\geq j$, and $d_{j,k}q_{N,j}=q_{N,k}$ when $j\geq k$.

Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves, scalar restriction, sheaf tensor, and K-flat derived change of rings [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $P$ be any K-flat $R$-complex [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The complexes $U_N=P\otimes_RB_N$ and $V_j=P\otimes_RD_j$ are K-flat over their respective coefficient sheaves. Their transitions $p\otimes x\mapsto p\otimes b_{N,M}(x)$ and $p\otimes y\mapsto p\otimes d_{j,k}(y)$ are semilinear chain maps. For every $eN\geq j$ there is a $D_j$-linear chain isomorphism
$$\theta_{N,j}:(U_N\otimes_{B_N}D_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}V_j,\qquad(p\otimes x)\otimes y\longmapsto p\otimes q_{N,j}(x)y,$$
with inverse $p\otimes y\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes y$. These chain isomorphisms commute with the semilinear transitions in both indices and with every chain map of K-flat $R$-complexes.

If $P$ has flat terms and represents $K\in D(R)$, localization of $\theta_{N,j}$ under the canonical K-flat computation isomorphisms is exactly the normalized target-valued comparison
$$(K\otimes_R^LB_N)\otimes_{B_N}^LD_j\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_R^LD_j$$
of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Consequently these derived comparisons are independent of the flat-term K-flat representative, natural in $K$, and compatible with every further reduction in either index. Neither flatness of the coefficient maps, nor boundedness or completeness of $P$ or $K$, is assumed.

proof.text: Obtain the family of ordinary and derived presentations p and its normalization ν from lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization. Apply lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings-all-independent separately to every beta_N and delta_j, using the object/map equations and additive instance of each presentation. This gives K-flatness without termwise flatness.

For composable a,b with a followed by b=c define coefficientStep by the ordinary adjunction unit for b whiskered by p(a), followed by restriction of the normalized cancellation theta. Its section formula is nu.ordinary_unit followed by nu.ordinary_hom at outer scalar 1. Define b and d by these coefficient steps. Define s by theta_Nj followed by the inverse of theta_Mj. Define t by the coefficient step from q_Nj to q_Nk whiskered by p(beta_N). All are actual natural transformations, so their degreewise lifts commute with differentials.

Equality transport of nu.ordinary_hom and nu.ordinary_inv gives precisely the forward and inverse tensor formulas for the given target delta_j. The s formula follows by applying theta_Mj to both proposed values: the cancellation formulas and q_Mj b_NM=q_Nj make them equal, and its inverse cancels. The t formula is coefficientStep_sections. The s comparison square follows directly by isomorphism cancellation. To prove the t square, use the two ordinary adjunction hom-equivalences to reduce equality of maps from the double extension to the tensors 1 tensor (1 tensor z). More generally its pure-tensor calculation uses q_Nj followed by d_jk=q_Nk and multiplicativity of d_jk.

Restrict each coefficient step back to R using nu.restrictionComp, whose sections are the identity. Pure tensors detect maps from this restricted extension: transport by p.obj_eq, use the sheafification hom-ext property, then tensor induction. On pure tensors composition of two restricted steps is the step for the composite coefficient map, and the identity coefficient map acts identically. The functor laws of B and D now give all four identity/composition clauses on arbitrary sections. For the mixed square use double-extension extensionality and the established s and t formulas; both composites have value d(y) tensor (b(x) tensor z).

Chain-map naturality is the naturality of the specified lifted natural isomorphism cofinalQuotientChainTheta. Substitute the equality beta_N followed by q_Nj=delta_j in nu.representative. The resulting representative identity is exactly the final clause, since cofinalQuotientTheta reduces to nu.ordinary for the composite. This retains the canonical derived computation and all universes and imposes no boundedness or coefficient flatness.

Steps 2-4 are elementary, and I re-checked them: R-balancing of the transitions via b∘β=β and d∘δ=δ; the R- and B_N-balancing of θ and the R-balancing of ι; both composites; and the first-index transition, well defined via q_{M,j}b=q_{N,j}. 'Extension in each tensor factor' is the scalar-restriction adjunction plus the sheafification universal property, which counts as elementary. Edge cases: Z→Z/4→Z/2 with P=Z; D=0; the contractible complex Z/2→Z/2, which has non-flat terms (the chain clause holds, and the derived clause is correctly restricted to flat-term P); identity indices.
